— Railroad crossings and work zones","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Railroad crossings and work zones

FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Open joints on bridges or ramps can throw a motorcyclist, so slow down for them [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Expansion joints bump traffic or cost traction in wet weather where they span the lanes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
An intersection warning sign means a junction is ahead: stay alert for vehicles entering your road [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A01
A Y intersection forces a right or left bear ahead, while a T intersection ends your road at a stop sign where you must turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A01
Roundabout signs announce a circular intersection with a center island and one or more lanes, where entering traffic yields to the circle and travels counterclockwise [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A01
A right curve with a side road means the road bends right while a side road joins from the left inside the curve: watch for entering vehicles [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: FXsec04F07
A sharp-right or sharp-right-then-left warning calls for slowing and preparation for abrupt turns. A right-then-left curve warning tells the driver to slow down [FXsec04F07].
Source: [FXsec04F07 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A01
A right curve with a safe speed indicator means slowing to that posted speed, and a winding road with its series of turns means slowing on every curve for control [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A01
A low ground railroad crossing warns that a steep slope can hang a low vehicle on the tracks [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A01
Advance railroad crossing signs tell you to look, listen, slow down, and stand ready to stop for trains or any rail vehicles [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A01
A crossbuck warns of the crossing itself: look, listen, slow, and prepare to stop, since trains may come from either direction and from either track at multi-track crossings [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A01
Where flashing lights join the crossbuck, stop when flashing starts and wait until every train or rail vehicle has passed, the tracks are clear, and the lights stop, watching for a second train from the opposite way [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F13 | anchor: A01
Where gates join the lights, stop when flashing starts before the gate falls, stay stopped until the gates rise and the lights stop, and never drive around a lowered gate [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec04-F14 | anchor: A02
An X with RR painted on the pavement may mark the approach to some crossings [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F15 | anchor: A02
Trains can reach a crossing at any time from either direction, so never start across unless you can clear the tracks completely with room waiting on the far side [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F16 | anchor: A02
School buses must always stop at railroad crossings, even when the lights are not flashing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F17 | anchor: A02
For a dangerous rail-crossing condition, call the number on the emergency sign and give the posted crossing number so rail traffic can stop or reroute [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F18 | anchor: A02
If your car stalls on the tracks, get out at once and run diagonally away from the tracks in the direction of the oncoming train [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F19 | anchor: A02
In work zones obey posted limits and shun distractions: speeding convictions can cost up to $500, handheld device use costs $250, and orange always means slow down and stay alert [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F20 | anchor: A02
Rough road, bump, and uneven lane signs warn of gravel or construction surfaces that trouble motorists and especially motorcyclists [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F21 | anchor: A02
Road construction and detour signs mean the traffic pattern or route is changing ahead: slow down for unusual or dangerous conditions [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F22 | anchor: A02
Large flashing arrow boards and message signs in work zones steer drivers into open lanes and announce closed road ahead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F23 | anchor: A02
Flaggers in orange or yellow vests or yellow-green shirts use STOP/SLOW paddles or red flags to stop and steer traffic so workers and equipment can cross [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F24 | anchor: A02
A photo speed enforcement sign means automated cameras ticket speeding in the work zone: always obey the posted limit [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec04-F25 | anchor: A02
Barricades, vertical signs, concrete barriers, drums, and cones guide work-zone lanes: hold the middle of your lane at the posted speed, and after the zone keep lane and speed until fully clear before changing lanes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0012]
